intro: I build computational methods for small-molecule design. My work sits between cheminformatics and machine learning: reaction-based enumeration for generating synthetically feasible analogs, structure-based modeling to evaluate new chemical series, and generative models for exploring chemical space.

Before moving into computational chemistry, I worked across computational biology — transcriptomics in cancer, and microbiome analysis in critical care. That background still shapes how I approach chemical data.

focus.title: Reaction-based enumeration
focus.detail: HEALER — retrosynthetic fragmentation and forward recombination to generate analogs a chemist can actually make.

focus.title: Structure-based modeling
focus.detail: Molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and protein–ligand modeling to design and evaluate chemical series.

focus.title: Generative & predictive ML
focus.detail: Diffusion models for structure-conditioned molecule generation, and ADME property prediction including cytochrome P450 activity.

education.institution: University of North Carolina – Chapel Hill
